subject.title: [Feature]: Compaction: configurable model override + flush-then-reset mode

question: Should OpenClaw add a built-in compaction-threshold flush-then-reset mode, and should it be unified with the reset-time memory flush policy tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/45608?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing the behavior affects config surface, silent model execution, provider/auth routing, memory persistence, reset latency, and session-state semantics.

options.title: Design one lifecycle policy
options.body: Approve one explicit memory-preservation policy covering compaction-triggered reset and reset-triggered flush, with opt-in defaults and security/latency constraints before implementation.

options.title: Keep reset work separate
options.body: Leave this issue open only for compaction-triggered flush-then-reset and handle manual/daily/idle reset memory through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/45608.

options.title: Do not add core reset mode
options.body: Keep the shipped model overrides as the supported cost-control path and reject flush-then-reset unless a plugin/API gap is identified.

recommendation.title: Design one lifecycle policy
recommendation.body: Approve one explicit memory-preservation policy covering compaction-triggered reset and reset-triggered flush, with opt-in defaults and security/latency constraints before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across pre-compaction memory flush, reset behavior, and current memory-flush recovery policy.
